reasoning: Hard gates fail: kelvin_ok=false, gates_pass=false, structural DRC=21. The critical new observation is that cable 2 has an ASYMMETRIC Kelvin failure: /SENSEC2_HI appears in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines but /SENSEC2_LO does NOT — meaning SENSEC2_LO is already routed while SENSEC2_HI is blocked. Because kelvin_unrouted only increments for pairs where BOTH members are unrouted, cable 2 contributes 0 to that metric (invisible to it). Rule 33 force-injects for symmetric/fully-unrouted pairs (kelvin_unrouted>0 targets cable 1 only); the compiler also bypassed SENSEC2_HI entirely this round — its 7 stubs targeted only /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA, all absorbed or spur-trimmed. Result: SENSEC2_HI received ZERO routing guidance in round 93 (no Rule 33 stub, no compiler stub) while remaining the sole blocker of cable 2's Kelvin gate. This gap is self-reinforcing: each round the compiler and force-injector ignore SENSEC2_HI, leaving it unrouted indefinitely. Additionally, 5 total unconnected ratlines (3 Kelvin-related + 2 non-Kelvin) and DRC=21 (just above the >20 trigger level for Rules 45 and 47) confirm shunt-cluster congestion persists. The diffpair gate passing is the only positive signal. Verdict: repair — the hard Kelvin and DRC gates both fail, and the asymmetric Kelvin gap means the current injection protocols will not self-correct on cable 2.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Raising from 700 to 800. The asymmetric Kelvin failure for cable 2 (SENSEC2_HI unrouted, SENSEC2_LO routed) contributes to the unconnected count but contributes 0 to kelvin_unrouted, which only counts symmetric pairs. The unconnected metric is the only existing scorer handle on asymmetric Kelvin members. Increasing its weight from 700 to 800 creates proportionally more scoring pressure on all unrouted ratlines — including asymmetric Kelvin members that fall through the kelvin_unrouted metric — without requiring a new metric key. The 100-point increase is deliberately modest; the manager rule below is the primary intervention.

manager_rule: Detect and force-inject for ASYMMETRIC Kelvin failures. After evaluating round R: for each cable index C, if exactly one member of the pair (/SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO) appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' while the other member does NOT appear in failing_reasons (partner is routed), AND that cable is NOT already contributing to kelvin_unrouted for round R (because kelvin_unrouted only counts fully-unrouted symmetric pairs where both members are absent): in round R+1, inject a force stub for the unrouted member only (the single member with unconnected ratlines) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, bypassing the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages for that stub. Do NOT inject a force stub for the already-routed partner member — injecting both would risk FR rerouting the established partner path to satisfy a competing stub geometry. This asymmetric single-member stub injection is additive to any Rule 33 symmetric force stubs and any compiler stubs generated for round R+1; it does not suppress compiler output or other force injections for that round. Log 'asymmetric_kelvin_single_member_force_inject' with fields: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) which member is unrouted (e.g. /SENSEC2_HI), (d) which member is already routed (e.g. /SENSEC2_LO), (e) stub coordinates injected for the unrouted member. Rationale: Rule 33 force-injects Kelvin stubs only for cables contributing to kelvin_unrouted (symmetric failures); an asymmetric failure where one member is blocked but the other is routed falls entirely outside Rule 33's scope and outside the compiler's normal priority if that net's absorption count is low but FR simply failed to route it. In round 93, SENSEC2_HI received zero routing guidance while remaining the sole cable-2 Kelvin gate blocker — a gap that will repeat every round without an explicit injection protocol for asymmetric cases.
